name: Rheon Systems SoftShell Ballistic Underlayer
description: Worn under civilian clothing, the SoftShell is a full-torso soft ballistic underlayer in off-white with Rheon's triple-hex pattern embossed subtly across the surface. The material is a non-Newtonian smart composite — pliable and light at rest, rigidifying on sudden impact across the strike zone. Slim enough to hide under a dress shirt or fitted jacket without obvious bulk. The neck and underarm panels are perforated for airflow. A faint chemical smell dissipates within an hour of first wear.
functionality: Rated for low-velocity ballistic and blade-edge impact across torso and upper back. Smart-stiffening activates on impact without requiring power. Chrome-port bypass channels route implant cabling cleanly through the torso without creating pressure points or ballistic weak spots.
what_it_says: You have enough enemies to warrant armor and enough taste to hide it.
story_hooks: A SoftShell was recovered from a crime scene with a strike deformation pattern that doesn't match any registered weapon caliber in the M88 database.
Rheon quietly recalled a batch of Mark IIIs for a stiffening failure — but the recall notice never reached the black market units already in circulation.
A corporate fixer was photographed at a peace summit — image analysis suggests they're wearing a SoftShell under diplomatic clothing, which is a treaty violation.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, minimalist torso garment that disappears under layers. Off-white with a barely-visible embossed triple-hex tessellation pattern creating subtle light-play across the surface. Fitted but not restrictive — designed for concealment beneath professional or casual wear without telltale silhouette.
physical_description.fit: Slim, body-conforming compression fit. Hugs the torso without compression restricting movement. Designed to sit flush under a dress shirt or fitted jacket with zero visible bulk or print-through.
physical_description.primary_material: Non-Newtonian smart composite (proprietary Rheon blend) — pliable and lightweight when at rest, capable of rigidifying on sudden impact across designated strike zones.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost slick surface with subtle embossed hex pattern that catches light at acute angles. Perforated underarm and neck panels have a softer, mesh-like texture for breathability. Overall feel is engineered rather than organic.
physical_description.color_scheme: Off-white (near-cream) as primary, with embossed triple-hex pattern in fractionally darker tone — creates relief only under certain lighting. No bright accents or branding visible on exterior surface.
physical_description.closures: None — designed as a slip-on full-torso underlayer. Seamless or minimal seaming to avoid detection.
distinctive_features: Embossed triple-hex tessellation pattern (Rheon Systems trademark, subtle)
Perforated underarm and neck panels for thermoregulation
Non-Newtonian impact-responsive zones across chest, flanks, and upper back
Minimal seaming; engineered for zero print-through under fitted garments
Faint chemical smell on first wear (dissipates within ~1 hour)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional tech. Affordable enough for working-class adoption, sophisticated enough to signal corpo-adjacent safety consciousness or corporate employee status.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by mid-tier corporate workers, security-conscious professionals, street fixers, and anyone in moderate-risk occupations. Signals pragmatic self-preservation without overt paranoia — 'I take reasonable precautions.' Common in GLMZ professional districts and mixed-tier neighborhoods.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine on first wear (with fading chemical smell). Remains crisp through standard washing. Over time, embossed pattern may slightly diminish; perforated panels retain texture. Rarely visibly damaged unless subjected to actual ballistic impact, at which point localized rigification leaves permanent stress marks in the composite.
